title: Soft value iteration and the Boltzmann optimal policy
brief: Replace the hard max with a soft one, find the soft-optimal Q on a random MDP and the frozen lake, check its Boltzmann policy against the soft Bellman equation, and watch it become ordinary value iteration as the temperature falls.
hints: soft_value is m + alpha * log(sum(exp((q - m) / alpha))) with m the row maximum. Without the shift, Q = 1000 and alpha = 0.01 overflow.
In soft_bellman_backup, set the soft value of terminal states to 0 before calling rlenvs.q_from_v. A row of zeros has soft value alpha * log A, not 0.

soft_policy_evaluation is rlenvs.policy_evaluation on a copy of the MDP whose reward is R - alpha * log(pi). Build it with rlenvs.TabularMDP(P=..., R=..., gamma=..., mu0=..., terminal=...), then turn V into Q with rlenvs.q_from_v on the original MDP. Treat log(0) as 0 when alpha is 0.
soft_bellman_residual uses soft_value(q[s2], alpha), the soft value of each next state, times (1 - terminated).
